Protecting sick employees is commendable and understandable. Sometimes things don't go your way.

But why put Dutch companies at such an enormous competitive disadvantage?

Sure, every country has its own system, so a one-to-one comparison isn't entirely fair. But a gap this extreme is hard to justify.

Why would any country choose this?

Crypto is taking off. So why aren't bags pumping?

Base's Jesse Pollak says this is what mainstream adoption looks like, with less than 1% of the world's dollars and equities onchain

"There's almost like a weird feeling at times in crypto over the last year, where I think people feel almost a dissonance of like, oh my god, it's so clear that we're taking off from a product market fit and growth perspective, but maybe this isn't what we expected, and maybe it's not pumping our bags."

"The way I look at this is, this is what mainstream adoption looks and feels like."

"When you have a technology that is getting adopted by the biggest financial companies in the world because it offers faster, cheaper, better financial services, I think that's the vision that we've been building towards now for 13 years."

"Look at stablecoins or look at equities. We have less than 1% of the world's dollars, less than 1% of the world's equities moving on these new rails."

"Over the next 5 years, 10 years, it's going to be about going from less than 1% to 10% to 50% to 90%, and that is just a massive, massive pie."

Do you know what Schwartzer means?

Half of my family, the Aldens, came over to the US on the Mayflower in the 1600s. John Alden, google him.

The other half was German, leaving after WWI for good reason. They were the Schwarzwalders, meaning the Black Foresters. That name means people of southern Germany’s Black Forest.

When that side came to the US, Ellis Island officials said the name was too long. It was changed from Schwarzwalder to Schwartzer at the border. Which means blacker/darker.

I am Lyn Alden of the Black Forest.

Lyn Alden the darker.

I discard nothing.

The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

The consumer is still strong even though their costs of housing have gone up. It's AI that's really helping us there, and everybody's hopeful at some point that we get costs down. That's the optimism that remains in the economy right now. 

Obviously, the administration can tell the success of the economy based on earnings, but earnings don't put food on the table. People in local regions in almost every state, and certainly the top 10 contested states, are being barraged by ads that say, "Look, everything's too expensive." But in Mid-America, or you're part of a small business which represent more than half the economy, you're feeling pretty good right now because your customer is still there for you. This is going to be a very close election, and will be based on how people are feeling about the future. It's always that way.

AI spending is rapidly accelerating in the US.

US private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software grew at an annualized rate of +7.3% in Q3 2026, to a record $1.77 trillion.

This marks the largest quarterly increase since Q4 1983.

By comparison, at the height of the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric grew +6.2%.

Since Q4 2022, private fixed investment in information processing equipment and software has surged +61%, or +$671 billion.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 5.4%, significantly surpassing the previous high of 4.5% recorded in Q4 2000.

The scale of US AI investment is unlike anything seen before.

BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$2.8 billion in September, or -2.1%, to -$134.9 billion, its widest gap since March 2025.

Imports rose +$8.1 billion, or +2.4%, to a record $344.2 billion.

This jump was led by a +7.5% MoM increase in capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment fueling the AI buildout.

Now, the capital goods deficit has widened by -$54.3 billion YoY, accounting for more than the entire increase in the overall trade deficit.

Meanwhile, US goods exports jumped +$5.3 billion in September, or +2.6%, to $209.2 billion, driven by a +12.8% increase in food shipments.

The US trade deficit is rapidly widening again.

posts.text:
Multiple roommates.  Ramen noodles.  Near public transportation.  Respect to the people who do whatever it takes.  

I worked as a bartender.  Bar-back. $2.15 an hr plus whatever tips got shared.  Worked at a retail store. Never had benefits at any job.  

Had 5 roommates in a 3 br apt.  Ate lousy food out of cans and ate  a ton of peanuts and shit food  at happy hour.  Had credit cards ripped up.  Etc.  

But I learned a ton.  Taught me what was right and wrong about running a business by watching my bosses and their bosses 

Yeah I know. It was much easier then, when inflation was 15 pct and national unemployment was 10 %.  I know I was fortunate when I finally got fired from the store, and had to start my own business with zero cash.   Bill collectors everywhere. 
Even luckier when I found my first customer so I could pay my bills

But I recognize it’s so much harder today.  

Which is why I respect the people who are willing to do what it takes to get started

posts.name: Steve Burns
posts.text:
One of the most useful things to measure after earnings isn't the size of the gap.

Measure how much of that gap survives.
A stock that gaps 12% and keeps 11% has processed the new information very differently from one that gaps 12% and finishes up 2%.

The announcement creates the gap.
The price action afterward tells you what traders ultimately decided about the move.
